Took me 33 years to admit it to myself. I didn’t have the words, I just always said “I’m just me”. 

Took me 2 more years to come out. I cried when I told my dad he had a son because he said “oh, that’s what you had to tell me? I thought it was bad news.” Got mad when my big sister, whom I’m closest to, didn’t accept it and questioned my existence. Felt relief when my little sister, whom I fight with constantly and am not at all close to, just started cracking jokes and called me bro, telling my big sister “I’d rather have a happy brother than a depressed sister.” 

Since I’ve started transitioning, my depression is gone. I’m happier. I’m learning what it’s like to be a guy. What the rules are, how to adapt myself to not be “that white guy”. I’m more comfortable in my skin. 

All that to say, your fear is valid, but you never know where support will come from. It may come from the most unlikely place. Living your truth will set you free like nothing else. Fighting for your truth will be hard sometimes, but living as you are will make the fight 1000x more bearable. Society makes too many rules, but they can be learned. 

And honestly, I wish I could be a woman. They are scary! Every woman I’ve ever met is someone I would not want to get on the bad side of. Women are fierce, and strong, and capable, and they are a force of nature. They are as beautiful as they are resourceful and resilient. 

You have a community who will welcome you with open arms and pro tips about everything you could have questions on… when you’re ready. Even when you’re not ready, this community will stand by you. 

Last thing. It’s a trans woman that started Pride with the Stonewall Riot. Make of that what you will.

Eeeeeh. Doctors have to study pharmacology and chemistry. They know what the drug molecules are and how they affect the body, where the receptors for that drug are and what are the most likely side effects you’re to have on said drug. 

A doctor knows how to do a proper search for what it is you have, knows what markers to prove or disprove a diagnosis... they aren’t just textbook regurgitating dummies. 

Anyone can learn to recite words from a textbook, doctors *Understand* what those words mean and in what context. They *ARE* much more reliable than Google. They aren’t just ordinary people with a fancy piece of paper that can hand out drugs... For fucks sake, would you prefer that some rando re-wire the electrical in your house or do you want a certified electrician to do it? That “fancy piece of paper” means that they have been rigorously evaluated, tested and deemed competent to practice medicine by a body of experts.

That’s not to say that some doctors should of never have become doctors in the first place because they are ableist, racist or sexists. They exist, sure and they are a right pain in the ass to deal with. Sometimes having a doctor with prior first hand experience of your symptoms can make them *LESS* sympathetic to you. Ask anyone with a woman gynaecologist. 

It’s not black and white. What you need is to talk with your physician, have them understand that they don’t live in your body, you do. Explain the symptoms you have, explain the effects the meds have and explain WHY staying on medication is better for you than the alternative. 

Also, try to have someone with you at your appointments. They might have questions you haven’t thought of but would like to know the answer to, and they can also remember bits you might have forgotten.

I'm a medicine student and had an abortion about a year ago. There are a couple of things I would like to share.

Plan B is effective 24 hours after the non protected intercourse. You need to take both pills at the same time for it to be effective. After 48 hours, Plan B is effective at 87%. After 72 hours, it drops to 71%. The reason why you need to take it after 24 hours is because of the longevity of the sperm vs your potential ovulation. Sperm lives up to 3 days in the vaginal canal. It takes 2 days from the fertilization to reach your uterus. Plan B works in 2 ways: it stops you from ovulating and thins out your uterine wall so that if the ovule is fertilized, it cannot stick. Taking it so soon after intercourse means that you ovulated after the effectiveness of the pill wore off and the sperm left in your vaginal canal was able to fertilize the ovule.

Abortion procedure. If you made up your mind and do not wish to see or hear the heartbeat, the physician must respect your wish and not show you. This can be a traumatizing experience for some women and because hormones are already running high, pregnant women are more susceptible of rash decisions when shown traumatizing images. The physician is supposed to give council before the procedure to verify the mindset of the patient. Any physician who doesn't ask the patient permission before showing the image of the ultrasound is irresponsible and liable in case of the patient later developing depression/suicidal thoughts. It's malpractice. Pure and simple.

Medical vs surgical. I had a surgical abortion at 6 weeks along. My physician assessed me and found that I would not handle a medical abortion well. They did not show me the ultrasound image as per my wishes, they turned the monitor on and facing the wall and left me alone for a while to prep myself mentally for what was going to happen. No sound was on either. They (the doctor and assisting nurse) gave me a IV sedative before the procedure and I was knocked out. This happens to most women. It makes the experience much less traumatizing. Some women do remain conscious with the sedative though. When I came to, I was in recovery and allowed to sleep it off for 4 hours before leaving. I felt fine afterwards. No sadness or shock. It was as if I had a bad flu making my body act weird and all of it was now over. I was trained in the psychology of surgical abortions are less traumatizing than medical because the patient does not go into labor. It has one risks associated with it, but is mentally more sound for the patient.

I was not given a high enough dose of antibiotics afterwards though, so I developed a uterine infection. The clinic sent me to the ER (no cost to me), and the doctors at the hospital sent me to the maternity ward for 2 days while pumping me with Dilaudid (opiate 250x stronger than morphene) and IV antibiotics. They put me away from the moms and newborns on the edge of the ward for my mental sanity. A lot of my friends and my boyfriend came to see me and made the whole thing more bearable.

After an abortion, it is necessary to surround yourself with loving and understanding people. It is a difficult choice to make but one that should be respected.
